squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition tells civilians to leave Yemen's Hodeidah port after Houthi attacks on Riyadh
squawks.detail: The coalition's Joint Forces Command published a call for civilians to evacuate the Red Sea port of Hodeidah, citing their safety. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: EU says terms of UK reset deal depend on UK charging EU students the same tuition fees as British students
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Andy Burnham is set to agree the deal, while the EU says its terms depend on the UK giving European students the same tuition fees as UK students.

squawks.headline: Hungary reportedly lifts its veto, letting Ukraine open the last two EU accession clusters
squawks.detail: Market reports say Hungary has withdrawn its veto, allowing Ukraine to open the final two clusters of its EU accession negotiations. No official confirmation was included in the reports.

squawks.headline: Traders scale back ECB rate-hike bets and now price only two hikes by the end of 2027
squawks.detail: Money market traders have reduced their bets on ECB tightening. Pricing now points to two rate hikes by the end of 2027.

squawks.headline: No.10 says UK–EU summit negotiations have concluded and the deal is done, with talks continuing in some areas
squawks.detail: Downing Street said the UK–EU summit deal has been agreed and both sides have settled when it will come into force, with the dates set out in a joint statement. Talks will continue on some areas.

squawks.headline: Estonia to shut its border crossings with Russia from 1 December and will review the closure after 6 months
squawks.detail: The Estonian government says its border crossings with Russia will close from 1 December onwards and that it will reconsider the decision in 6 months.

squawks.headline: Polish general says 11 objects threatened Polish airspace and 3 of them crossed into it
squawks.detail: General Nowak of Poland's military gave the figures on Friday as the incursion story continued, after Poland said missiles and a drone that came down on its territory came from Russia.

squawks.headline: Poland says two missiles and a drone that came down on its territory came from Russia and will ask NATO for more support
squawks.detail: Poland's defence minister said a Russian KH-101 cruise missile likely fell in Poland, called it another Russian provocation and linked its timing to a meeting of the coalition of the willing. He said Poland will ask NATO for additional support.

squawks.headline: ECB's Santos Pereira says the ECB will keep acting decisively on rates as inflation risks increase
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Santos Pereira said inflationary pressure is significant, risks are rising and the ECB will continue to act decisively on interest rates.

squawks.headline: UK Business Secretary says the aim of the EU reset is now to stop new trade barriers from emerging
squawks.detail: The Business Secretary described the goal of the Burnham-led UK–EU reset as preventing new barriers to trade. A UK politics journalist noted that this differs from the broader options set out at party conference.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Russia will not win the war and links Ukraine aid and investment to reforms
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said he had told Ukraine that fast-moving reforms are the basis for investment and financial aid. He also said Russian hybrid attacks on Germany are increasing every month.

squawks.headline: ECB's Santos Pereira says energy-driven inflation pressures are still significant
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Santos Pereira said energy is still driving significant inflation pressures. He said the key question is whether energy price pressures spread to the rest of the economy.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia starts refilling joint crude storage in Japan, and Japan plans to buy 8m barrels of Saudi oil for its own reserve
squawks.detail: Saudi state news agency SPA says Japan will offer 16m barrels of oil storage and Saudi Arabia has begun refilling the joint crude storage in Japan. Separately, Japan plans to buy 8m barrels of Saudi crude for its own reserve, and both countries stressed the importance of a stable oil market.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde names AI combined with cyber threats as the challenge that worries her most
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said the combination of artificial intelligence and cyber threats is the challenge that concerns her most. She made no reference to rates in the reported remarks.

squawks.headline: EU and UK agree a youth mobility scheme for 100,000 young people from each side, EU official says
squawks.detail: An EU official says the EU and the UK have agreed a youth mobility scheme for 100,000 young people from both sides. The agreement comes on the day of the UK–EU reset summit.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says the ECB's swap lines will become easier to access
squawks.detail: ECB President Christine Lagarde said the central bank's swap lines will be made more accessible. No further details were given in the report.

squawks.headline: European bond sales go above €2 trillion for the first time
squawks.detail: Bond issuance in Europe has passed €2 trillion for the first time, according to a market newswire report.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's nuclear plants reduce output after Russian strikes on energy grid, with outages in Kyiv and ten regions
squawks.detail: Ukraine's deputy energy minister says the nuclear power plants cut output after Russian attacks on energy distribution. He says the overnight strikes caused power cuts in Kyiv and ten regions.

squawks.headline: Burnham is set to sign the UK–EU reset deal in Brussels, covering freer food and drink trade and a youth scheme
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Burnham will sign the UK–EU reset agreement in Brussels. The deal provides for closer ties, including freer trade in food and drink and a youth experience scheme.

squawks.headline: French Budget Minister Amiel says an extra €6bn budget effort is only a starting point for 2027
squawks.detail: France's Budget Minister Amiel described the additional €6bn of budget effort as a starting point for 2027 fiscal plans. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French overall business climate slips to 95 in November, below the 96 forecast, while the manufacturing index reaches 104
squawks.detail: France's overall business climate index fell to 95 from 97, compared with a forecast of 96. The manufacturing index was 104, down from 105 but above the 103 forecast.

squawks.headline: ONS revises UK April–September borrowing down by £3.6bn, citing stronger tax receipts
squawks.detail: With the October public finances release, the ONS lowered its estimate of the 2026/27 deficit for April to September by £3.6bn. It put the revision down to stronger tax receipts data.

squawks.headline: UK and EU expected to agree easier food trade and youth mobility at Friday's reset summit, with divisions still in place
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Britain and the European Union are expected to agree to ease food trade and youth mobility at a summit on Friday as part of a reset of ties. The report adds that the summit is also likely to show disagreements that remain over the longer-term relationship.

squawks.headline: ONS says UK supermarkets reported stronger October sales after government advice to buy long-life items
squawks.detail: The ONS gave the supermarket comment alongside the October retail sales release.

squawks.headline: German producer prices rise 8.1% year on year in October, above the 7.3% forecast
squawks.detail: German PPI rose 1.4% on the month against a 1% forecast and 1.9% previously; the annual rate rose from 6.7% in September.

squawks.headline: Swedish seasonally adjusted unemployment falls to 8.2% in October, below forecasts
squawks.detail: The seasonally adjusted rate fell from 8.6%, against forecasts of 8.55% to 8.6%; the unadjusted rate was 7.7% against 8.1% previously.

squawks.headline: UK public sector net borrowing comes in at £17.0bn in October, below the £18bn estimate and down from £24.5bn
squawks.detail: ONS data show October PSNB ex banking groups at £17.036bn against an estimate of £18bn and £24.52bn the previous month. The public sector net cash requirement was £10.8bn and the central government net cash requirement £15.5bn, both against £16.9bn previously.

squawks.headline: UK retail sales rise 0.7% on the month against a flat forecast, and core sales gain 0.9%
squawks.detail: Headline UK retail sales rose 0.7% month on month, against a 0% forecast and -0.4% previously, and were up 2.3% year on year, against 1.7% forecast and 0.8% previously. Core sales rose 0.9% on the month, against 0.1% forecast and -0.7% previously, and 2.5% on the year, against 1.8% forecast and 0.8% previously.

squawks.headline: Russia's foreign ministry says there is no agreement yet on the next round of Ukraine talks
squawks.detail: Russia's foreign ministry said no date has been agreed for further Ukraine negotiations, according to Interfax. Separately, the ministry said Moscow is preparing to host European Union representatives.

squawks.headline: Sri Lanka's central bank governor says rate cuts will resume after inflation moves lower
squawks.detail: Sri Lanka's central bank governor said the bank will go back to cutting rates now that inflation has fallen. No timing or size of cuts was given in the report.

squawks.headline: South Korea's KOSPI closes down 5.21% at its weakest level since 16 January
squawks.detail: South Korea's KOSPI index ended Friday's session 5.21% lower, its weakest close since 16 January, as the sell-off across Asian markets continued.

squawks.headline: Gold heads for its worst week in eight months as a firm dollar and bets on a December Fed hike weigh
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that gold slipped on Friday and was on course for its worst week in eight months. It says a resilient US dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December weighed on prices.

squawks.headline: UK Business Secretary Reynolds says UK tariff decisions will serve UK industry, not simply follow the EU's lead
squawks.detail: Business Secretary Reynolds said the UK would set tariff policy in the interest of its own industry rather than copying EU measures, and that both sides stand to gain a lot from EU-UK trade. He also said financial services were neglected in the original Brexit negotiations.

squawks.headline: Oil rises on supply worries after Houthi attacks on Riyadh and reported tanker disruption in Hormuz
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that oil prices rose on Friday after Houthi attacks on the Saudi capital and reports of tanker disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. Prices were still on course for a weekly fall.

squawks.headline: BoJ policymakers mostly agree a rate hike is needed next month but differ on how far rates should rise, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Bank of Japan policymakers broadly back a rate rise next month. They are split on where rates should eventually peak.

squawks.headline: Russia carries out its biggest strikes on Kyiv's bridges of the war and hits energy infrastructure, and Kyiv brings in emergency blackouts
squawks.detail: Kyiv's mayor said a Russian ballistic missile attack hit three bridges over the Dnipro and killed three people. Russia's defence ministry said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure, and city officials introduced emergency blackouts.

squawks.headline: Japan's 40-year government bond yield falls to 4.150%
squawks.detail: The 40-year JGB yield fell to 4.150% during the Asian session as Japanese equities sold off.

squawks.headline: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 and the Nikkei falls 5% as the dollar holds near a 19-month high
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Asian shares fell on Friday as the AI sell-off deepened, and Japan's Nikkei fell 5%. The dollar has risen for eight sessions on safe-haven flows and is near a 19-month high.

squawks.headline: Japan's 2-year government bond yield slips to 1.835%
squawks.detail: The 2-year JGB yield fell to 1.835% in Asian trading. A JGB re-offer auction earlier produced a highest yield spread of -0.017%.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson says shared understanding of the outlook matters more than explicit rate guidance
squawks.detail: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson repeated on Thursday that the Fed will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high. She also argued that a shared understanding of the outlook matters more than explicit guidance on rates, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: China, Russia and the US are linked to a proposed joint declaration on global peace, SCMP reports
squawks.detail: The South China Morning Post reports that Beijing, Moscow and Washington are linked to a proposed joint declaration on global peace. Singapore's prime minister separately praised Xi after what was described as a landmark trilateral summit with Washington and Moscow.

squawks.headline: Yen firms as Japan's core inflation accelerates in October and stays above the BoJ's 2% target for a second month
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Japan's annual core inflation picked up in October and was above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for the second month in a row. The yen strengthened on renewed expectations of a BoJ rate rise.

squawks.headline: Citi underestimated its risk-weighted assets by $35bn after a trade-recording error, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters cites sources as saying the error in recording some trades forced Citigroup to inject capital into a subsidiary.

squawks.headline: US Senate passes a bipartisan energy permitting bill by 62 votes to 33
squawks.detail: The US Senate approved the cross-party energy permitting legislation 62-33.

squawks.headline: Asian markets sell off as Taiwan's Taiex falls more than 6% and Korea triggers a KOSPI circuit breaker
squawks.detail: Taiwan's benchmark fell more than 6%, the Korea Exchange triggered a KOSPI circuit breaker, Japan's broader index fell 3%, the Hang Seng fell 2% and Shanghai fell 2%. Spot gold fell nearly 2% to $3,551.75/oz and LME copper fell 3%.

squawks.headline: Canada's LeBlanc says Washington has shown little movement on easing US tariffs, sources say
squawks.detail: Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the briefing, that Canada's minister for US trade told an advisory committee on Thursday that Ottawa is still seeking an interim arrangement but the US has shown little movement.

squawks.headline: China leaves its 1-year and 5-year loan prime rates at 3.00% and 3.50%, in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China kept both benchmark lending rates unchanged for an 18th consecutive month, matching expectations. The central bank also added 379.5bn yuan through overnight reverse repos at 1.25%.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr warns that regulatory changes underway at the Fed may raise financial sector risks
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Michael Barr said on Thursday that changes to US financial regulation could make it harder to spot and respond to future market stress, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: JGB yields fall, with the 20-year down 3.5bp at 3.685%, as the Nikkei drops 4.5%
squawks.detail: The 5-year JGB yield fell 2.5bp to 2.195%, and Japanese bonds were reported to be tracking strength in US Treasuries. Asian equities opened lower amid global risk aversion, and Taiwan's benchmark index fell more than 4%.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson says steady long-term inflation expectations reflect Fed credibility and wage growth is consistent with 2% inflation
squawks.detail: Paulson described wage growth that fits with 2% inflation as a positive sign. These remarks follow her earlier call for more tightening.

squawks.headline: RBA's Fry-McKibbin sees pockets of strong Australian demand alongside weakness amid a large global oil supply shock
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia monetary policy board member Fry-McKibbin made the remarks, describing the global oil supply shock as huge.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson says more tightening is needed and calls cutting inflation the top priority
squawks.detail: The Philadelphia Fed President said inflation remains elevated with the labour market at full employment, and that a gradual pace of rate increases gives the economy time to adapt.

squawks.headline: Japan's economy minister says underlying inflation is quickening as firms pass on Middle East-driven costs
squawks.detail: Economy minister Kiuchi said wages and prices are rising steadily together and household income remains resilient, while rising inflation expectations are weighing on consumer sentiment.

squawks.headline: UK GfK consumer confidence rises to -22 in November from -24, in line with forecast
squawks.detail: The GfK consumer confidence index came in at -22 in November against a poll of -22, up from -24 in October. The major purchases gauge rose 5 points.

squawks.headline: Japan's October CPI rises 2.3% year on year, below the 2.5% forecast, as core measures also undershoot
squawks.detail: Headline CPI rose from 2.1%, CPI excluding fresh food was 2.2% against a 2.3% estimate, and CPI excluding fresh food and energy eased to 2.2% from 2.4%. The 10-year JGB yield was later reported 2bp lower at 2.800%, and the 40-year yield fell to 4.155%.

squawks.headline: Canada's LeBlanc expects US tariffs on autos and steel to remain as Ottawa pursues a comprehensive trade deal
squawks.detail: Canadian minister Dominic LeBlanc said he expects the US tariffs on autos and steel to stay in place while Ottawa seeks a comprehensive trade solution with Washington.

squawks.headline: Israel's spy chief reportedly urged renewed strikes on Iran during a visit to the US, WSJ says
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Israel's intelligence chief pressed for fresh strikes on Iran while visiting the US. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin invites European leaders to Moscow for talks on ending the Ukraine war but signals no softening of Russia's demands
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin has invited European leaders to Moscow to discuss a resolution to the war in Ukraine. His remarks indicated that Russia is not prepared to ease its hardline conditions for ending the conflict.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says inflation has been more persistent than thought, citing data centre demand, AI wealth effects and demand pressures
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said inflation had been far more persistent than expected in 2025, with data centre demand and AI-related wealth effects adding to it, and that price pressures include a sizable demand component as well as oil and tariff shocks. He said he is not concerned about wages pushing up inflation at this point, and that the Anthropic IPO raises questions about how shareholders will spend their wealth, which could have a macroeconomic impact.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign ministry says US claims about Iranian chemical and biological weapons are meant to justify military action
squawks.detail: A spokesman for Iran's foreign ministry said on X that US accusations of chemical and biological weapons development aim to spread fear and build a case for military action against Tehran.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says he does not see US inflation on a path back to 2% and links the rate path's steepness to that return
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said inflation has been far more persistent than thought in 2025, with demand adding to oil and tariff shocks, and that the past few months have not brought good news on inflation. He said he is not concerned about wages adding to inflation and warned that the current level of business investment carries a high risk of overheating.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says services inflation is key to judging whether price pressures come from demand or energy costs
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said in remarks on Thursday that services inflation trends help show whether price pressures come from demand or from factors such as energy costs.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Iran war came up in talks with Putin and Xi, and both want it to end
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the war with Iran was discussed with Russia's President Putin and China's President Xi, and that both leaders want the conflict to end. The remarks were reported by an NBC reporter.

squawks.headline: US Senate rejects resolution to limit Trump's war powers on Iran, 48 votes to 51
squawks.detail: The US Senate voted down a war powers resolution on Iran that would have removed US armed forces from hostilities with Iran, by 48 votes to 51 once all votes were counted.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr says inflation is still too high and further monetary policy adjustments are needed
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said inflation remains excessively high, financial conditions are still accommodative and supporting the economy, and policy adjustments are still necessary. He also said the AI surge is part of a risk-on market climate, that easing regulation in such an environment can cause problems, and that the Fed is not targeting a specific level of investment.

squawks.headline: Trump says Putin wants a deal on Ukraine and hopes Zelensky does too
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks in an interview reported by Fox News, following his call-in to the Berlin leaders' meeting on Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr says his disclosed disagreements on bank oversight centre on long-term challenges with bank rules
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said the disagreements over banking oversight that he has disclosed relate to long-term challenges with bank rules. He added that he is concerned the direction of regulation could make financial risks harder to understand.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr says AI may raise the risk of faster bank runs
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said AI could widen access to financial services but must comply with financial sector rules, and may increase the risk of faster bank runs.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says second-round inflation effects are likely and the Bank must shore up its inflation credibility
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said second-round effects on inflation will probably occur and that the Bank needs to strengthen its credibility on inflation. The remarks add to her earlier comments today on the labour market and policy restrictiveness.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says labour data point to slower disinflation and the labour market is less weak than thought
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said labour market data indicate disinflation is slowing. She added that the labour market has not been as weak as the Bank had thought.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says policy has been less restrictive than thought, pointing to above-target inflation and a resilient economy
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said there is a question over how restrictive monetary policy has been and that it has not been as tight as previously thought. She cited inflation running above target and economic resilience.

squawks.headline: South Africa's central bank keeps its key rate on hold in a split decision
squawks.detail: The South African Reserve Bank held its key interest rate on Thursday in a split vote, Reuters reports. Its governor said policy was tight enough after two hikes this year.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says the risk of doing too little outweighs doing too much and inflation expectations must be anchored at 2%
squawks.detail: MPC member Megan Greene said the Bank has a duty to anchor elevated inflation expectations at the 2% target and that people notice when inflation is above 3%. She said the risk of underacting is bigger than the risk of overdoing it.

squawks.headline: Canada seeks an interim trade arrangement with the US by the end of the year, CBC reports
squawks.detail: Canadian broadcaster CBC reports that Canada is seeking an interim trade arrangement with the US by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's Zelensky says leaders will not travel to Moscow
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said leaders will not go to Moscow. He spoke as talks on ending the war in Ukraine continue.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's Zelensky says Kyiv needs 70bn more in financing and hopes the war ends before 2028
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Kyiv needs a further 70bn in financing and dozens of F-16 jets, and that no date or venue has been set for the next round of talks. He said he hopes the war will end before 2028.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's Zelensky sees a real opportunity to end the war but warns this winter could be the hardest yet
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said any Russian discussion of territory must be held with him directly, and that a deal requires a peaceful Europe. The remarks came as the leaders of Germany, France, the UK and Ukraine issued a joint statement calling on Russia to agree to a winter energy ceasefire.

squawks.headline: UK, German, French and Ukrainian leaders urge Russia to accept a winter energy ceasefire as a first step to ending hostilities
squawks.detail: A joint statement from the leaders of Germany, France, the UK and Ukraine asks Russia to agree to an energy ceasefire lasting through the winter, as a first step towards a cessation of hostilities. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: UK, German, French and Ukrainian leaders pledge extra missile defence for Ukraine before winter and binding security guarantees
squawks.detail: In a joint statement, the leaders of Germany, France, the UK and Ukraine say Russia cannot outlast the coalition's support. They pledge extra efforts to supply Ukraine with more missile defence before winter, and say robust, legally binding security guarantees must be in place once a ceasefire takes effect.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim several high-profile military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis announced a number of high-profile military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia. This follows an earlier Houthi attack on Riyadh's financial centre, which Saudi Arabia condemned.

squawks.headline: Trump says any Iran decision will wait to see what happens after the start of next year, Axios reports
squawks.detail: Axios reports that US President Trump said he is not rushing into a decision on Iran and will see what happens after the beginning of the year.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the Fed still wants evidence that AI productivity gains are spreading beyond tech
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the Fed is still looking for signs that AI-driven productivity gains are reaching beyond the tech sector. He said that if they do not, AI could turn out to be a short-lived boost.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says oil flow out of Hormuz was the largest yet yesterday and sees no rise in Iran tensions
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said the previous day had seen by far the largest flow of oil through the Strait of Hormuz. He also said there was no increase in tensions over Iran.

squawks.headline: Trump says he is in no hurry to decide on Iran, Israel's Channel 12 reports
squawks.detail: Israel's Channel 12 reports that US President Trump said he is in no rush to make a decision on Iran. The same outlet earlier reported that he had discussed the possibility of an attack on Iran.

squawks.headline: US 10-year TIPS auction tails by 0.3bp at a 2.903% high yield, with bid-to-cover at 2.43
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $19bn of 10-year TIPS at a high yield of 2.903%, up from 2.653% at the previous sale. The when-issued yield was about 2.90% before the auction. Bid-to-cover was 2.43 against 2.240 last time, and 90.74% of bids were awarded at the high; primary dealers took 6.03%, direct bidders 25.41% and indirect bidders 68.56%.

squawks.headline: ECB's Panetta says policymakers must fight inflation without doing too much damage to growth
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Panetta said inflation must be tackled without hurting growth too much, adding to his earlier remarks on stopping inflation from becoming entrenched.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the Fed cannot look through tariffs if they persist and sees no stagflation for now
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the Fed's failure has been on inflation rather than the job market, and that he does not currently see stagflation. He also said shifts in immigration policy mean the Fed should give monthly jobs data less weight as a signal of the business cycle.

squawks.headline: US gas exporters grow more willing to sign long-term European deals after EU delays methane law
squawks.detail: A senior US gas industry official told Reuters that exporters are more comfortable signing long-term contracts with European buyers. This follows EU lawmakers agreeing to delay a new methane emissions law further.

squawks.headline: Trump discusses the possibility of an attack on Iran, Israel's Channel 12 reports
squawks.detail: Israel's Channel 12 reported that US President Trump discussed a possible attack on Iran. The report follows earlier news that the White House had asked the Pentagon to assess scenarios on Iran.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the Fed's job now is to stop the AI surge overheating the US economy
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said greater hype around AI companies pulls more demand and investment into the present. He added that the Fed has fallen short on inflation but he does not see stagflation now.

squawks.headline: ECB's Panetta says inflation must be stopped from becoming entrenched
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Fabio Panetta said policy must prevent inflation from taking root. He gave no further detail in the reported remarks.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee is concerned that tariffs are pushing up inflation for longer than expected
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the effect of tariffs on inflation has lasted longer than expected. He also said AI looks promising for productivity, but the Fed's job is to judge whether the economy is overheating now.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says US consumer demand has been very strong and solid
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee made the remark in the same comments in which he said the job market is stable and inflation is well above the 2% target.

squawks.headline: Polish PM Tusk says Poland will not send troops to Ukraine after hostilities end under the coalition of the willing plan
squawks.detail: Russian media reported the remarks. Tusk was commenting on NATO exercises currently taking place in Poland.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the US job market is stable but inflation is well above the Fed's 2% target
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the labour market is steady while inflation remains far higher than the 2% target, according to a market newsfeed.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says Ukraine's security guarantees will be Article Five-based and Russia has been made comfortable with that
squawks.detail: Speaking in Berlin, US peace envoy Kushner said an Article Five-like guarantee is a big deal that Trump is open to, provided it is in the US interest. He also stressed the importance of having the right communication channels.

squawks.headline: J.P. Morgan now expects the Fed to raise rates by a quarter point in January and March, adding to the December hike it already forecast
squawks.detail: J.P.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen says a 22nd package of Russia sanctions is coming and points to a new €45bn loan for Ukraine
squawks.detail: The European Commission President spoke after the Coalition of the Willing meeting. She said the EU will keep increasing pressure on Russia until it comes to negotiations.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says NATO will be a central pillar of any post-war Ukraine settlement
squawks.detail: Speaking in Berlin, the US peace envoy said any deal will be made in close consultation with Ukraine and Europe, and that Trump wants Europe beside him for a deal.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says Russia has agreed to multilateral talks with Europeans and calls the Berlin talks on Ukraine successful
squawks.detail: Speaking in Berlin, US peace envoy Kushner said Russia has agreed to engage in a multilateral format with the Europeans, Trump is open to security guarantees and there has been progress on a post-war prosperity plan and on Ukraine's pathway to the EU. He also said peace will be hard to achieve but that a sovereign Ukraine is achievable.

squawks.headline: Pentagon official puts the cost of the Iran war at more than $48bn
squawks.detail: A Pentagon official said the US conflict with Iran has cost more than $48bn so far.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says Russia's demands are unrealistic, pledges lasting support for Ukraine and calls for a push to peace with US involvement
squawks.detail: UK Prime Minister Burnham said the aggressor should not be setting wide-ranging demands, that the UK will step up again and stay at Ukraine's side for as long as it takes. He said this should be a moment to move towards peace with US involvement.

squawks.headline: France's Macron calls for reopening the question of Ukraine's NATO membership and says the coming weeks are critical for Kyiv
squawks.detail: French President Macron said the issue of Ukraine's place in NATO must be put back on the table, and described the next few weeks as critical for Ukraine. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: France's Macron says Ukraine's allies must give Kyiv what it needs now and work on helping to protect the capital
squawks.detail: French President Macron said leaders gathered in Berlin spoke with Trump through his envoys on Thursday. He said Ukraine's allies must do everything they can now to supply what it needs and must work on helping to protect Kyiv.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's Zelensky says Europe must take part in the next round of talks with Russia
squawks.detail: Ukrainian President Zelensky said on Thursday that the next round of talks with Russia has to include Europe.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says sanctions on Russia could be lifted on conditions if progress is made, and calls Moscow's maximalist demands unrealistic
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said Russia knows its maximalist demands are not realistic and that sanctions could be lifted conditionally if there is progress. He also said Washington can rely on Germany's cooperation as long as their goals stay the same.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Europe broadly agrees on financial backing for Ukraine and rejects a Yalta-style format for peace
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said Europe has wide consensus on financially backing Ukraine and that Germany will support it for as long as needed. He also said a Yalta format would not bring peace to Europe and described the leaders' meeting in Shenzhen as mainly a photo opportunity.

squawks.headline: Polish PM Tusk says Russia is unlikely to be ready for peace talks before the end of winter
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Russia is unlikely to be ready for Ukraine peace talks before winter ends. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says he discussed more Chinese purchases of US farm goods with Xi but is non-committal on soybeans
squawks.detail: NBC reports that President Trump said he spoke to China's President Xi about buying more US agricultural products. He did not say clearly whether Xi had agreed to buy more soybeans.

squawks.headline: US Kansas City Fed manufacturing index rises to 23 in November from 16
squawks.detail: The Kansas City Fed's manufacturing index came in at 23, up from 16 the previous month. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: US Kansas City Fed composite index rises to 18 in November, above the 10.5 forecast
squawks.detail: The Kansas City Fed manufacturing composite index came in at 18, against a forecast of 10.5 and a previous reading of 11.

squawks.headline: Trump says Putin told him he is angry about the Crimean Bridge attack
squawks.detail: US President Trump said Putin had expressed anger over the bridge attack, according to NBC. Putin earlier ruled out negotiations after the attack.

squawks.headline: Trump says he agreed with Zelensky that no decisions on Ukraine will be made without Ukraine taking part
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump said he and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky agreed that decisions about Ukraine should not be made unless Ukraine takes part, according to reports.

squawks.headline: Fed's Jefferson says he has no interest in changing the inflation target
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said he is not interested in changing the Fed's inflation target. He made the comment in the same appearance as his earlier remarks on AI and energy-driven inflation pressure.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia condemns the Houthi attack on Riyadh and reserves the right to take all necessary measures
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry condemned Houthi attacks on civilian and economic facilities, including Riyadh's financial centre. It said the kingdom reserves the right to take all necessary measures to defend its sovereignty.

squawks.headline: Trump joins leaders' meeting on Ukraine in Berlin by phone and is reported optimistic about peace after talks with Putin
squawks.detail: Trump called in to a leaders' meeting in Berlin on Ukraine and told them he had spoken with Putin, according to sources. The sources said he expressed optimism about peace.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence says a Houthi attack hit a tower in Riyadh's financial centre, damaging several floors
squawks.detail: Saudi civil defence attributed Thursday's attack on a tower in the Riyadh financial centre to the Houthis and said it damaged several floors and nearby buildings, with no injuries reported.

squawks.headline: US leading economic indicators fall 0.3% in October against expectations of no change
squawks.detail: The Conference Board's US leading economic index fell 0.3% month on month in October to 99.3, against a consensus of no change and an unchanged reading the previous month.

squawks.headline: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli says the Bank will act as needed to hit the CPI target
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor and MPC member Clare Lombardelli said the Bank will take whatever action is required to meet its CPI inflation target.

squawks.headline: US extends deadline for talks on sale of Lukoil International's foreign assets to 19 December
squawks.detail: A US statement extended until 19 December the deadline for talks on selling the foreign assets of sanctioned Russian oil producer Lukoil's international unit, Lukoil International GmbH. This follows the US Treasury's earlier Russia-related general licence covering dealings with the company.

squawks.headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says she hopes to reach a trade deal with the US at the December G20 summit in Miami
squawks.detail: Mexico's president said she hopes to agree a trade deal with the US at the G20 summit in Miami in December. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Treasury issues Russia-related general licence 131l permitting some dealings involving Lukoil International GmbH
squawks.detail: The US Treasury has issued a Russia-related general licence, numbered 131l, that authorises certain transactions involving Lukoil International GmbH.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC says there will be no nuclear talks until the Strait of Hormuz issue is resolved
squawks.detail: A spokesman for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Iran will not discuss its nuclear file until the Hormuz issue is settled, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported.

squawks.headline: Fed's Jefferson says AI buildout is adding to inflation pressure and an energy shock forces inflation-jobs trade-offs
squawks.detail: Fed official Philip Jefferson said in prepared remarks that the AI buildout affects both demand and supply, with the current pressure falling on demand, and that the energy cost shock creates trade-offs for central banks between inflation and employment risks. His text did not comment on the interest-rate outlook.

squawks.headline: NAO overview of HMRC puts tax revenue at £966.4bn and the tax gap at £59.2bn
squawks.detail: The National Audit Office has published its latest overview of HMRC, covering £966.4bn of tax revenue, a £59.2bn tax gap and plans for £886m of efficiency savings. The report also looks at HMRC's work to modernise its technology and customer services.

squawks.headline: IEA chief calls the Strait of Hormuz crisis the biggest threat to energy security in history
squawks.detail: The Executive Director of the International Energy Agency said the Hormuz crisis is the largest energy security threat on record and that, if it continues, it will reshape countries' energy policies, according to reports.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields trim gains after data; 10-year up 1.85bp at 5.085%, 2-year up 3.21bp at 4.832%
squawks.detail: US Treasury yields gave back part of their earlier rise after the release of US economic data. The 10-year yield was 1.85bp higher at 5.085% and the 2-year was up 3.21bp at 4.832%.

squawks.headline: US Philadelphia Fed business index falls to 6.3 in November, far below the 20.1 forecast
squawks.detail: The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index came in at 6.3 for November, against a forecast of 20.1 and 20.9 the previous month.

squawks.headline: US initial jobless claims rise to 203K, above the 197.5K forecast
squawks.detail: US initial jobless claims were 203K in the week to 14 November, up 1K from a prior week revised to 202K from 200K. Forecasts cited ranged from 197K to 198K.

squawks.headline: US continuing jobless claims rise to 1.763M, above the 1.7025M forecast
squawks.detail: US continuing jobless claims came in at 1.763M, compared with a forecast of 1.7025M and 1.697M in the previous reading.

squawks.headline: France and UK clash over food rules before an EU summit as talks on Britain's role in shaping regulations go to the wire
squawks.detail: The FT reports that France and the UK disagree over whether Britain should be able to influence EU food regulations, with talks continuing up to a key EU summit. This follows reports that PM Burnham is due to sign a deal aligning the UK with EU food standards.

squawks.headline: APEC leaders call for uninterrupted energy flows and resilient supply chains, and warn global imbalances threaten growth
squawks.detail: According to Xinhua, APEC leaders committed to keep energy flowing without interruption, make supply chains resilient, cooperate on global rebalancing and cross-border data, and invest in tech infrastructure. They also said global imbalances threaten growth.

squawks.headline: Kremlin's Peskov says the US broadly backs a mission to Konstantinovka but Kyiv has not responded
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the United States has generally supported the idea of a mission to Konstantinovka, while Kyiv has given no response, according to reports.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia considers the deployment of any foreign troops into Ukraine unacceptable
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin restated his opposition to any foreign troop deployment in Ukraine, TASS reported. He also said living conditions in a security zone on Russia's border with Ukraine would match those in the rest of Russia.

squawks.headline: Putin says the EU is turning into a military-political bloc and calls this a challenge for Russia
squawks.detail: In further remarks, President Putin also said Russia has opened a route to Crimea through Novorossiya and will strengthen its presence there after the attacks on the Crimean Bridge. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin says relations with Europe cannot be fully restored unless political leadership changes in some European countries
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin made the remarks during his ongoing comments on relations with Europe and the Ukraine settlement. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia is not preparing for war with Europe in 2030 and that such plans keep being talked about in the EU
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said Russia has no plans for a war with Europe in 2030, and that it repeatedly hears the EU talking about such plans. He made the remarks as he continued to comment on Ukraine settlement talks and European security.

squawks.headline: Putin says the US keeps pressing Russia to admit Europeans to Ukraine talks, and Europeans have been invited to Moscow
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said Washington has repeatedly urged Moscow to accept European participation in Ukraine negotiations, and that Europeans were invited through diplomatic channels to come to Moscow and explain what they would bring to trilateral talks. He also said Ukraine's security must be part of the wider European security framework.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia is ready to continue Ukraine settlement talks but no dates are set, and Europe must take part in security talks
squawks.detail: The Russian president said Russia wants to end the Ukraine conflict and is open to a new round of negotiations, though no dates have been agreed, Interfax reports. He also said security talks would be pointless without Europe, that normal dialogue with Europe must come first, and that Ukraine's aim of keeping the remaining 10% of Donbas it holds is pointless.

squawks.headline: White House asks the Pentagon to assess scenarios on Iran, Axios reports
squawks.detail: The White House has asked the Pentagon for assessments of possible scenarios involving Iran, according to Axios. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin says a new European security system can be achieved and accepts Ukraine's right to security if it does not cost Russia's
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said a new European security system is achievable, Interfax reported. He also said Ukraine has a right to security but not at the expense of Russia's, and that returning to the geopolitical realities of the 1990s makes no sense.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US will see what happens in its conflict with Iran after 1 January
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the comments in remarks broadcast on Thursday, Reuters reports. He did not say why the date mattered.

squawks.headline: Putin says the Crimean Bridge strike has ended talk of a partial ceasefire and calls territorial pressure on Russia pointless
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said, according to TASS, that the strike on the Crimean Bridge seriously damaged its road section and ended discussion of a partial ceasefire. He also said efforts to pressure Russia on territory were pointless and that Ukraine has the same right to security as Russia.

squawks.headline: Putin rules out negotiations after attacks on the Crimean Bridge and vows a much more painful Russian response
squawks.detail: Putin said he had discussed a possible ceasefire in some areas with Russia's Security Council, but that Russia would hold no negotiations after the attacks on the Crimean Bridge. He also said the bridge's railway section had already been restored and that it had not been used to carry military equipment or petroleum products.

squawks.headline: Putin says Ukraine and Europe are not yet ready to compromise on a settlement and Russia accepted US proposals in Anchorage
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said Russia agreed in Anchorage to compromises proposed by the US on Ukraine, but Kyiv and Europe are not yet willing to make concessions, although that could change later. He added that Russia is ready to discuss settlement terms with its partners, Interfax reports.

squawks.headline: Putin expects Russia-US moves to restore relations to continue and says a partly implemented deal beats having no deal
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said he expects the momentum towards restoring Russia-US relations to continue and that some decisions will also be taken in other formats. He also said an agreement that is not fully implemented is better than none, and that Russia's demands on European security are legitimate even though they have not been clearly set out.

squawks.headline: Putin says he discussed freedom of navigation with Trump and Xi and sees Trump as committed to settling the Ukraine conflict
squawks.detail: Speaking after the three-way meeting with the US and Chinese leaders, Russian President Putin called the meeting useful, Interfax and other outlets report. He said he wants better US-Russia ties and that agreements with the US are hard to follow through on, but the Trump administration's approach gives grounds for optimism.

squawks.headline: Putin says he wants the three-way meetings with the Chinese and US leaders to continue
squawks.detail: At a press briefing, Russian President Putin said he would like the Russia-China-US leaders' meetings to continue and called the trilateral summit a chapter in the history of diplomacy, RIA and Interfax report.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the US is considering increasing diesel and oil exports to Europe
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in Warsaw that the US is weighing a step-up in diesel and oil exports to Europe. The posts report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: China-US-Russia leaders' meeting covered Ukraine, Iran, the Korean peninsula and nuclear proliferation, Chinese state media says
squawks.detail: Chinese state media listed Ukraine, Iran, the Korean peninsula and nuclear proliferation as the topics of the three-way meeting between the leaders of China, the US and Russia. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran looks to be getting ready to restart oil shipments, according to TankerTrackers
squawks.detail: Tanker-monitoring service TankerTrackers reports signs that Iran is preparing to resume oil exports. No market reaction was reported in the post.

squawks.headline: Bundesbank expects German growth to pick up in the fourth quarter and says higher rates will weigh on investment and construction
squawks.detail: The Bundesbank says German economic growth should speed up in the fourth quarter. It also says higher interest rates will hold back investment and construction.

squawks.headline: China, US and Russia issue joint peace declaration that includes a plan to raise refined fuel production and supply
squawks.detail: Chinese state media report that the joint statement from the three leaders sets out plans to increase both production and supply of refined petroleum products. The statement also restates that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

squawks.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin agree to increase supply of refined oil products
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that the Chinese, US and Russian leaders agreed at their three-way meeting to raise supplies of refined oil products. The report gives no figures or details of how this would happen.

squawks.headline: Russia, US and China leaders are due to issue a joint statement within the hour, Interfax reports
squawks.detail: Interfax reports that the leaders of Russia, the US and China are expected to release a joint statement within an hour, following their three-way meeting at the APEC summit.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says the ECB may have to adjust rates further after its two hikes
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said further rate adjustments may be needed after the ECB's two increases, according to a market news post. He spoke on the same day as his earlier remarks that a hike would send a clear signal.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says a rate hike would send a clear signal and sees no wage-price spiral
squawks.detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel also said he is confident the ECB will reach its 2% inflation target.

squawks.headline: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to Chinese customers under a new US rule, FT reports
squawks.detail: According to the FT, the two chipmakers have paused some shipments while they apply for US Commerce Department licences. Projects for ByteDance and Kunlun at Samsung Foundry and production of Xiaomi consumer chips at TSMC are reported to be on hold.

squawks.headline: Air strike hits headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that an air strike hit the headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. The attack comes after Houthi rebels fired at the kingdom almost every day. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: France sells 4-, 5- and 8-year OATs at higher yields than previous sales, with stronger bid-to-cover ratios
squawks.detail: The 4-year OAT went at 4.09% (previous 4.01%) with cover of 2.83 (previous 2.32), and the 5-year at 4.26% (previous 4.16%) with cover of 2.819 (previous 2.3). The 8-year went at 4.67% (previous 3.88%) with cover of 3.053 (previous 2.69).

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says there are no signs of second-round inflation effects so far
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said he does not yet see second-round effects in inflation. This follows his earlier remarks that eurozone inflation is still too high and that oil is pushing it up.

squawks.headline: BoE forecasts point to the UK's longest stretch without inflation below 2% since the early 1990s, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: A Reuters report says Bank of England forecasts show Britain facing its longest run without inflation falling below 2% since the early 1990s. Economists quoted in the report say this risks weakening public faith in the Bank's ability to control price growth.

squawks.headline: Xi proposes a China-US-Russia crisis prevention mechanism and says the three countries should be partners
squawks.detail: At the three-way meeting with Putin and Trump, Chinese President Xi said the three countries should set up a crisis prevention mechanism and that major powers should respect each other and coexist peacefully, Xinhua reported. He also called for non-interference in other countries' internal affairs.

squawks.headline: Xi tells Putin and Trump that nuclear war cannot be won and calls for a full ban on nuclear weapons
squawks.detail: China's president made the remarks at the three-way meeting with the US and Russian leaders, Xinhua reports. He called for nuclear weapons to be comprehensively banned and destroyed.

squawks.headline: OBR chair Haskel says UK labour market weakness stems mainly from falling labour demand and global instability, not AI
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility chair said this in an interview clip published by the IFS. He said AI could bring significant change in future but is not the main cause of the current weakening in the UK jobs market.

squawks.headline: Trump tells Xi and Putin at three-way meeting that their countries are best placed to discuss nuclear weapons
squawks.detail: US President Trump spoke at a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin, saying the three countries are in a unique position to hold talks on nuclear weapons. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Riksbank Governor Thedeen says the Swedish economy is performing increasingly well
squawks.detail: The Riksbank governor said the Swedish economy is performing increasingly well. The report gave no further detail.

squawks.headline: Xi, Putin and Trump meet at APEC; Xi and Putin say the three powers share responsibility for global peace and stability
squawks.detail: Chinese state media reported Xi as saying the world stays peaceful when major countries are in harmony and falls into chaos if they fight, and that the three countries should jointly safeguard peace and stability. Interfax reported Putin as saying Russia, China and the US can strengthen global stability if they cooperate constructively, while Trump said peace is never forged by declining opportunities.

squawks.headline: Putin says talks with Trump should cover global and regional ties and energy security; Trump raises nuclear arms reduction
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said the agenda with Trump should include global and regional relations and energy security, Interfax reported. Trump said the two had already covered a lot and were in a position to discuss cutting nuclear weapons, though he added that giving them up is very hard.

squawks.headline: China describes the Xi-Trump meeting as positive and constructive
squawks.detail: China gave its assessment of the meeting between President Xi and President Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit. A China-Russia-US summit in Shenzhen is also under way.

squawks.headline: Strike by workers cuts French nuclear output by 2.1 GW, EDF data show
squawks.detail: EDF data show that French nuclear generation has fallen by 2.1 GW because of strike action by workers.

squawks.headline: Xi urges the US to act correctly on Taiwan and calls on both sides to stop US-China tensions from escalating
squawks.detail: Xinhua reports that China's President Xi told the US to avoid major disruptions over Taiwan and said both countries should implement the leaders' consensus, widen cooperation and stop tensions escalating. He also said China and the US should prevent security risks from AI and keep it under human control.

squawks.headline: Xi says China will step up communication with the US on trade and AI
squawks.detail: Chinese President Xi said China would strengthen communication with the US on trade and artificial intelligence, Xinhua reported. The remarks follow his meeting with President Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

squawks.headline: Xi tells Trump that China and the US agree to draw up an action plan for a constructive, stable strategic relationship
squawks.detail: At his meeting with the US President, China's President Xi called for more cooperation and fewer disputes between the two countries, and for the recent positive momentum in relations to continue, according to Xinhua. He also said the two countries will cooperate on AI safety risks.

squawks.headline: German government confirms it has reached an agreement with UniCredit on Commerzbank
squawks.detail: Germany confirmed an agreement with UniCredit over Commerzbank on Thursday morning. No terms were given in the report.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says the conditions for using ECB tools to support France are not currently met
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said the criteria for deploying ECB instruments on France are not met at present. He had earlier said France cannot ignore its high debt and deficit.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says France cannot ignore its high debt and deficit
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said France must face up to the reality of its high public debt and deficit.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says eurozone inflation remains too high and oil is still pushing it up
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said on Thursday that inflation is still too high and that oil continues to drive it.

squawks.headline: Japan PM Takaichi says Tokyo's Taiwan policy is unchanged and in line with the 1972 agreement with Beijing
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said Japan's position on Taiwan is consistent with its previous stance and the 1972 agreement with Beijing. She also said Japan must strengthen its defence capability and will keep explaining its national security stance to other countries.

squawks.headline: US dollar reaches a 19-month high after Fed minutes point to more hikes; Australian dollar hits 10-month low on soft jobs data
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the US dollar rose to a fresh 19-month peak on Thursday after Federal Reserve minutes and hawkish remarks from a Fed official signalled further rate rises. The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low after weak Australian jobs data.

squawks.headline: Japan PM Takaichi says Tokyo has been in contact with Beijing over China's rare earth export controls
squawks.detail: Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi said Japan has been talking to China about its rare earth export controls. She also said Japan's interests will stay protected despite the US-China-Russia summit.

squawks.headline: Long-dated JGB yields fall, with the 30-year down 6.5bp to 3.990% and the 40-year down 5bp to 4.180%
squawks.detail: The 30-year Japanese government bond yield declined 6.5bp to 3.990% and the 40-year yield dropped 5bp to 4.180% in Asian trading.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US and China have reached a more balanced tariff arrangement and Xi backs keeping oil flowing through Hormuz
squawks.detail: After a two-hour conversation with Xi at the APEC banquet on Wednesday night, Trump said both sides had worked towards a fairer trade arrangement and that he plans to press Beijing to buy more US agricultural products. Xi said a China-US relationship built on strategic stability would be unprecedented and committed to continued cooperation.

squawks.headline: Kremlin calls Putin-Trump talks positive and says Ukraine was the main focus; Trump plans trilateral talks with Xi and Putin
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the meeting covered the Ukraine conflict and bilateral relations, according to IFX and TASS. Trump said he intends to discuss ending the Ukraine war with Xi first and then hold trilateral talks with the Chinese and Russian leaders.

squawks.headline: Trump and Xi meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit to discuss trade tensions and export curbs
squawks.detail: Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that the US and Chinese presidents met at APEC in Shenzhen, and the FT reported that trade tensions and export curbs were on the agenda. Trump also met Russia's Putin at the summit, saying the meeting could produce many positive outcomes.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham is to sign a deal aligning Britain with EU food standards to remove barriers to trade, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Prime Minister will sign an agreement that requires the UK to align with EU rules in the food sector in order to remove barriers to trade.

squawks.headline: IEA calls the Iran war the largest oil supply shock since 1970 and says the policy response could cut oil demand by 4% by 2035
squawks.detail: The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that the Middle East conflict has caused the biggest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade. It said world oil demand could fall by more than 4% by 2035 if governments speed up electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching in response.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia launches airstrikes on Sanaa after a Houthi missile threat causes damage in Riyadh
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it had dealt with a Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh and that falling debris caused material damage. The Houthi-run Saba news agency then reported Saudi airstrikes on Yemen's capital.

squawks.headline: BoJ Governor Ueda says deflation risk is lower and the Bank's JGB holdings should fall steadily as purchases taper
squawks.detail: Ueda said rates need to reach positive levels so that real rates can fall in a downturn, and that next year's wage talks are key to judging whether core inflation stays at 2%. He also said strong global demand is lifting Japan's exports and capital spending, and pushing up prices across a wide range of goods.

squawks.headline: EU Parliament and Council agree to delay methane monitoring and reporting rules for fossil fuel importers by two years
squawks.detail: The European Parliament said it had agreed with the Council to push back the methane monitoring and reporting deadlines that apply to energy importers by two years.

squawks.headline: China's Xi criticises Western protectionism at APEC and calls for free trade and open markets
squawks.detail: Chinese President Xi Jinping told APEC that countries should promote free and open trade, advance regional trade pacts and work on regional energy and food security. He pledged $20 million for APEC cooperation, and spoke shortly before US President Trump arrived in Shenzhen.

squawks.headline: BoJ Governor Ueda says the Bank has no current plan to reassess the pace of its ETF sales
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said the central bank does not currently intend to review the schedule for selling its ETF holdings.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva says rising global inflation calls for tighter monetary policy in many economies
squawks.detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said higher global inflation is increasing the need for monetary tightening across several economies. She also cited energy supply shocks and AI-driven demand pressures, and urged countries to build digital infrastructure faster.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva says energy supply and demand shocks are pushing global inflation to 4.7%
squawks.detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said shocks to energy supply and to demand are behind global inflation reaching 4.7%.

squawks.headline: BoJ Governor Ueda warns a weak yen could push inflation above target and says the pace and timing of hikes depend on the outlook
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said firms are more willing to pass on costs, so currency moves could affect core inflation and long-term inflation expectations more than before, and higher crude prices and a weak yen could squeeze household real incomes. He said the pace and timing of rate rises will depend on how likely the baseline projections are to materialise, that the right response is hard to judge if weak demand and a falling yen occur together, and that the BoJ's smaller presence in the JGB market lets long-term yields reflect market views.

squawks.headline: China threatens to retaliate against US curbs on remote access to advanced chips
squawks.detail: Beijing criticised Washington's moves to restrict remote access to advanced semiconductors and threatened retaliation, Semafor reports. The trade dispute comes ahead of a Trump–Xi–Putin summit in Shenzhen.

squawks.headline: Moody's expects the US to keep its record of highly effective monetary policy led by an independent Fed
squawks.detail: Moody's gave the view in commentary on the US economy, alongside its expectations that 2026 growth beat forecasts and that Congress will raise or suspend the debt limit.

squawks.headline: Poll: 86% of economists expect the BoJ to raise its rate to 1.50% in December
squawks.detail: In an economists' poll, 86% expect a December hike to 1.50%, and nearly 60% expect a further 25bp rise to 1.75% by end-March 2027. 83% said recent stock market volatility does not change the timing of the next hike.

squawks.headline: Moody's expects slower US growth as higher rates, elevated energy prices and a cooling AI investment cycle weigh
squawks.detail: Moody's says higher interest rates, elevated energy prices and the normalisation of the AI investment cycle will contribute to slower US growth.

squawks.headline: Moody's says US growth in 2026 beat its expectations and expects Congress to raise or suspend the debt limit in time
squawks.detail: Moody's said the US economy has grown more strongly in 2026 than it first expected, and that it expects Congress to raise or suspend the debt limit before the Treasury runs out of borrowing capacity, possibly after long negotiations. It also said it expects the US to keep its record of effective monetary policy under an independent Fed.
